turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: The team wants everyone to create an account before seeing appointments. They say it will make the journey easier to track.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: For whom?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: For the organisation, certainly. It could also help patients manage requests. But I haven't checked what it costs to get in.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: That's our question today. A promising metric can show one kind of success while concealing another kind of failure. We'll use six lenses to decide what quality means here.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: First: outcome. Are more people reaching appropriate care, not just finishing registration?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Yes. Usability?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Can they get through identity checks, recover a password, and fix a mismatch without losing the request?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Context?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Someone may need care urgently, have weak connectivity, or not control an email address.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Inclusion?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Test assistive technology, language, digital confidence, and an equivalent route to a person who can help.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Agency and trust?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Explain why identity is needed and what data is collected. Don't require an account just to learn whether the service can help.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: And service value?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Can staff keep the records accurate? What happens to support demand, duplicate identities, and maintenance?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: So, ban accounts?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: No. Let people browse services and broad availability first. Ask for identity when they submit or manage a request, explain why, and keep a phone route.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: How will you know that choice holds up?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Measure access to care, not only sign-ups. Watch abandonment, account recovery, support calls, identity errors, and differences across groups. Record who owns the trade-off and when we review it.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: That's the foundation we've built: the experience brief, usability scorecard, experience goals, context scenarios, service blueprint, and quality decision log. Next we'll look at human perception, which complicates every one of them.
